edition: Independent-referee revision. Run at the immutable Git commit linked in the article. All file paths, including input hashes, are relative to that checkout. Each entry identifies source and/or derivation labels in certificates/statement-index.tsv. Only entries explicitly marked historical refer to older printed numbers.

ordinary_filter_map.necessary_condition: Enumerate square-free 1≤q<r, 1≤B, 8≤qB²<r. Skip a prime q at B=1. As q=1 forces all b≥3 in the ordinary search, excluding B=3 excludes every possible occurrence of codegree nine. The older nine caps in the kernel are unreachable in this mode.

Integer interval b≥last, L²<Eb²≤(h+1/36)L² for h unused nonunit positions. Update L to kL and E to k²E−(L/g)² with g=gcd(b,L), k=b/g. Every nonunit degree has at least two different prime factors, so d≥6. The rank bound on primes is 2r+1. A new odd prime outside qL must be ≤h+1; direct interval and smooth-product enumeration use the same allowed-prime mask.

At an odd p in the support a nonunit denominator b is eligible iff p divides qb². Put m=(p−1)/2. A run of equal denominators of length n supplies at most floor(n/m) packets. Only the last run can extend. Require one m-run for each p. At p∤q require 2m eligible labels; if no 2m-run can form, require capacity for at least three packets. When 3|q require six packets, otherwise when 2|q four. The terminal native independent count requires at least p−1 denominators divisible by p at odd p|M, p∤q.

When the first run is still open and f=8, omit multiplicity f−1 at r≥20, use the relaxed cap 5 at r=23 and cap 2 at r≥24. For r≥24 require at least four possible dimension primes (2 and three odd primes). At r≥26 apply m≤f−1−(p−1)/2 for odd p exactly dividing f. For f=16,25,27 exclude m≥f−1 when f(r−f)≥25. Thresholds choose when to use a necessary bound; smaller ranks may retain more profiles.

For r≥23 and h=3,4 augment the current prime mask by {2,3} or {2,3,5}. At most two possible support primes falls in the two-prime family. With three remaining and exactly three possible primes including two, cap the dyadic exponent by [2|q]+2v₂(L)+2[E odd]; a cap ≤5 is in the ordered cone. With h=2 the new scale k is coprime to 10: for a possible three-prime support, a 2- or 5-exponent at positions 1,2,3 bounded by 5,4,3 is covered.

Set M=kL. Require 6≤d≤e, d,e|L, (k,de)=1, Ek²=1+d²+e², (k,10)=1, chronological denominators, and ≥2 prime factors in every nonunit degree. Each p|M has ≥2 nonunit degrees prime to p. Use the narrow next-denominator interval b≤floor(sqrt(73L²/(36E))) or a join on e² modulo E when it is wide. At h=2 primes of k are contained in supp(qL)∪{3}. The row is restored to increasing degree order and rechecked.

For r≥27, 3|q and 3∤z, closing the run at z overrides no inherited demand. After serving the required terms, send twice the least nonnegative residual modulo three to 2z. A passed demanded denominator or demand exceeding remaining slots rejects. Unused terminal tile constraints may be tested later.

At q=1 the only early (number of fours, number of fives) near-full endpoints tested are (1,23),(2,21),(3,20),(5,17),(7,14),(10,9),(12,6),(14,3),(15,1). The residual permits no further five. At ≥14 leading fours the two prefix patterns with two fives, or one five and three sixes, also drop out for the completed ordinary ranks ≤30.

For a square prefix beginning with four, write i=#4 and j=#5. At i=13,j≥4 use the thirteen-four Gauss row (a fifth five would exceed the mass). At i=11,j≥6 use the eleven-six result, including the j=7 branch. Once the prefix passes five, j=1 requires r≥23+i. At j=2,3,6,7 the other multiples of five including the vacuum must carry ≥(2,3,2,2)/25. Bound this mass by both the unspent mass and the known plus remaining-slot mass, with vacuum ≤1/5400². Reject only on strict inequality. The alternative q>1 rule for ranks 30/31 refers to the complete independent nonsquare partition. The completed rank-30 archive includes the 149 nonsquare lists in addition to its recorded theory leaves.

Regenerate the GMP root manifest (depth one through rank 27; saved depth and all-four refinement through 17 in the larger returns). Check key coverage, repeated keys, subtree coordinates and every formerly split child at its actual depth. Native integer overflow delegates only disjoint prefixes or retries the full shard in GMP. Each computed leaf needs a completion marker. The theorem-leaf test recomputes the stated predicate. Compare sorted whole degree lists, completeness markers and counts before applying the terminal screen.

Recompute complementary packet capacity, generator activity at an actual prime, and the regular-indicator divisor in this order. The fiber size includes the dyadic torus if 2|q; for odd D an eligible p-packet costs (p−1) labels. The regular-indicator test is for the ordinary category.

Test a divisor-closed dimension family, the defect-one multiplicity cap, defect-one block tiling and odd-valuation active/principal slice masses, followed by feasibility of joint masses. For family branches the square-free decoration and every divisor are quantifiers; finite cofactor promotion returning no proof keeps the branch.

For each odd r and support primes p,t different from r, demand an available pair with r∤d_X, p∤d_Y, required squared codegree divisibilities, and g=gcd(d_X,d_Y)≥2 with r≤max(5,(g−1)g²). At f=16 test the principal dyadic row by denominator lcm, its minimum lcm cost, integer traces, parities, norm and modular inequality; upper bounds round upwards.

At f≤120 test necessary integer trace rows. The position in “trace at degree j” indexes distinct nonunit degrees in decreasing order. Apply local multiplicity, parity and three-divisor bounds at f=8 (ordinary f=9 already absent); partition each degree multiplicity into feasible Galois-orbit sizes for f≤120. Larger codegrees are retained by these tests. For a surviving top degree n even, D=12n² and ternary profile 10n,2(n/2), test the mixed row. Finally test balanced phase masses at even-valued odd primes. A crossed-fiber state space >100000 or unhandled high phase skips that extra test.

Enumerate only q>1 from the complete initial range. The parity kernel also uses P+H≥6 when 2|q and an even-valuation odd p is present, and the integral demand of odd-length odd-denominator runs versus even-denominator orbits of length 4^v₂(b). The stated stronger dyadic checks apply to the ordinary table. Root manifests list actual executable and counts for each q,B.

Each q=1 slice enumerates B from its lower bound through floor(sqrt(r−1)). B≥5 at r=30–35; M≡2 mod 4, B≥5 at r=30–38 (4|L prunes, terminal M=kL must be 2 mod 4); B≥6 at r=37–45. The B=4 case is impossible with M≡2 mod 4. The odd M branch uses the separate odd bound. Remaining ranks below each interval are covered in the proof; a slice asserts no unrestricted completion there.

Use half-rank, table dimension Δ=D/2, the reduced gcd/energy constraints, and the special three/four rows. A covered dimension must be the full 2Δ. The ordinary no-nine, regular-indicator and full dyadic tests are absent.

Use w=2, odd denominators ≥1, d≥15 and r≡q mod 8. The required length of a run of pairs is divisible by 2^(min v₂(p−1)−1) across p|qb² and the product of eligible odd defect-one block sizes. At f=25,27 the saturated run is excluded. Require at least two p-free pairs (four when p=3 via the dimension sum mod 3). Variable heights and fixed support branches use p-free pair requirements and eligible packet counts. In the exactly-three-prime support the dimension exponents must reach (6,5,4) in order. A nonunit degree contains ≥2 distinct primes, limiting how many prime-free witnesses it can supply. Upper-round each reciprocal-square weight to the next 2⁻⁶⁴ grid point. The optional two-prime intersection test starts at cap 75, above the two cited ranges. Work limits widen the surviving set.
